title: Higher-order Stirling-number monotonicity and log-concavity conjectures
statement:
Let $S(n,k)$ denote the Stirling numbers of the second kind, and let $\mathfrak{S}_{1}(n,k)$ be the quantity defined by the paper's equation defining $\mathfrak{S}_{1}(n,k)$. Recursively define

$$
\mathfrak{S}_{\ell+1}(n,k)=\mathfrak{S}_{\ell}^2(n,k-1)-\mathfrak{S}_{\ell}(n,k-2)\mathfrak{S}_{\ell}(n,k)
$$

and, for $n\geq k\geq \ell+2$, define

$$
\mathcal{S}_{\ell}(n,k)=\frac{\mathfrak{S}_{\ell+1}(n,k)}{\mathfrak{S}_{\ell}(n,k)}.
$$

**Higher-order Stirling-number conjecture.** The following claims are valid: (1) for fixed $ell\in\mathbb{N}$ and $n\geq \ell+3$, the finite sequence $\{\mathfrak{S}_{\ell}(n,k)\}_{\ell+1\leq k\leq n}$ is logarithmically concave in $k$; (2) for fixed $n\geq k\geq 3$, the finite sequence $\{\mathfrak{S}_{\ell}(n,k)\}_{1\leq \ell\leq k-1}$ is strictly increasing in $\ell$; (3) for fixed $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ and $n\geq k\geq \ell+1$, the sequence $\{\mathfrak{S}_{\ell}(n+m,k+m)\}_{m\geq 0}$ is strictly increasing in $m$; (4) for fixed $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ and $k\geq \ell+1$, the sequence $\{\mathfrak{S}_{\ell}(n,k)\}_{n\geq k}$ is strictly increasing in $n$; (5) for fixed $n\geq k\geq \ell+2$, the sequence $\{\mathcal{S}_{\ell}(n+m,k+m)\}_{m\geq 0}$ is strictly increasing in $m$; and (6) for fixed $k\geq \ell+2$, the sequence $\{\mathcal{S}_{\ell}(n,k)\}_{n\geq k}$ is strictly increasing in $n$.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2040

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).
source_name: Feng Qi, “Diagonal recurrence relations, inequalities, and monotonicity related to Stirling numbers”, arXiv:1402.2040 (2014).
